# WrapYourGit: full description

> WrapYourGit turns a developer's GitHub activity for one year into an animated, shareable story. Free, read-only GitHub sign-in, no access to source code. Edition: 2026. Site: https://wrapyourgit.habibiahmada.dev

## What it is

A web app. You sign in with GitHub, WrapYourGit reads the activity counts GitHub keeps for your account for the year, and plays them back as a short story set to music, chapter by chapter, at your own pace. Its promise is that every number on screen is correct and explainable: each metric has a written definition, and anything GitHub does not provide is shown as unavailable rather than as zero. Estimates are labelled.

## The story

Three short warm-up slides, then nine chapters (about one minute of music), then a comparison with last year, a letter, and your downloads.

1. Intro: the first week of your contribution graph lights up.
2. Contributions: total contributions, active days and longest streak.
3. Rhythm: your year as a contribution calendar, your busiest month and weekday pattern.
4. Languages: the languages you wrote, weighted by your own commits to each repository rather than by repository size.
5. Projects: your most active repositories, new repositories and repositories you contributed to.
6. Community: stars and forks your repositories gained this year, and the most starred one.
7. Engineering: pull requests opened and merged, reviews and issues.
8. Identity: your developer archetype and the facts that earned it.
9. Closing: your handle, four headline facts and the year as a small graph.

After the chapters: this year against the same stretch of last year (fair while the year is still running), and a letter from Cell, the mascot, that reads your year the way a friend would. A quiet year is told it counts; a relentless one is told to rest.

## Archetypes

One main archetype plus up to two runner-ups. If none fits yet, the story says so.

- Builder: created at least two repositories, or made 50 or more commits to your own.
- Consistent: active on at least 30% of the days so far.
- Explorer: wrote in four or more languages.
- Collaborator: ten or more reviews, or ten or more pull requests on other people's repositories.
- Night owl: at least 40% of sampled commits between 22:00 and 04:00 (estimated, and labelled as such).
- Open sourcer: contributed to three or more public repositories you don't own.

## What you can keep

- The story itself, in the browser, with its soundtrack.
- Ten slides as PNG (1080 × 1350, one per chapter plus the letter), or all ten in a ZIP.
- One PDF with the same ten slides.
- A public page at /<your-username>, built from public activity only, for every GitHub username; private repository names never appear, and the owner can hide it in Settings.
- An MP4 video in four aspect ratios: coming soon, not available yet.

## Privacy

- Reads: counts GitHub already keeps about your year (contributions, languages, repositories you committed to, stars, pull requests).
- Never touches: your code. Signing in asks GitHub for no repository permissions.
- Token: kept on the server only, encrypted at rest, never sent to the browser.
- Public: a recap of your public activity at /<your-username>, open to anyone like your GitHub profile. It drops private repository names, your timezone and the hours you commit. Settings has a switch to hide it.
- Leaving: Settings, then Delete my data, removes your account and recap, hides your public recap and revokes WrapYourGit's access to GitHub.
- Full policy: https://wrapyourgit.habibiahmada.dev/privacy

## FAQ

**Does WrapYourGit read my code?** No. Signing in asks GitHub for no repository permissions, and it only reads the counts GitHub keeps about your activity.

**Why is my active-days number slightly different from my GitHub profile?** Your yearly total matches the profile. On a few days GitHub's public graph files one contribution on the neighbouring day, so active days can differ by one or two.

**Are private repositories included?** Your contributions to private repositories, your own and your organisations', count toward your total. Their names never appear in anything you can share.

**2026 isn't over yet. Is my recap final?** Not until the year ends. Until then the story says "so far", and you can sync again from your dashboard to bring it up to date.

**Does it compare with last year?** Yes. Your dashboard and the story put this year next to the same stretch of last year.

**Can I download the video?** Not yet. MP4 export is still being set up. Today you can download every slide as a PNG, all of them as a ZIP, or one PDF.

**Can anyone open a recap of my username?** Yes. Like your GitHub profile, a recap of your public activity is open to anyone at /your-username. It never names private repositories. To hide it, sign in and turn on Hide my public recap in Settings.

**How do I delete my data?** Sign in, open Settings and choose Delete my data. It removes your recap and account, hides your public recap and revokes WrapYourGit's access to GitHub.
